drafted_from: tool:add-a-pooled-result's and tool:withdraw-pooled-results' own rows (their words, input schemas and steps, retired in this commit) and tools/learn-from-everyones-results read-data/pooled-results.mjs; the proof is the recipe's prove step, run on PGlite and a JSON folder.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-pooled-results with store {\"where\":\"postgresql database example_pool on my own computer\",\"language\":\"SQL (PostgreSQL)\",\"credential_name\":\"example-pool-postgres-connection\"} and results [{\"contributor\":\"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa\",\"situation\":\"sample-situation-1\",\"worked\":true}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the pool results and shared situations are kept in the pool's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the pool's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the pool is and how it is spoken to.

2. Say "Run workflow:keep-pooled-results" with store, and results (each one person's randomized yes or no at a shared situation, with their random contributor id) and withdraw (contributors whose every result is removed) as you want them kept.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: every answer must be the one the intent says, or the run stops and says which.
4. Read what came back: added, removed, and each refused item with its position and why. Nothing is changed for a refused item.

worked_examples.title: Keep one randomized result at a shared situation on its sample
worked_examples.ask: Keep one person's noisy yes or no about a shared situation in the pool everyone learns from, under their random contributor id

store.where: postgresql database example_pool on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The shared situation sample-situation-1 is kept in the pool at version 1, with no result from this contributor yet.
worked_examples.hands_back: added 1, removed 0, refused [], and a pooled-result record kept under the contributor's id at version 1.
